name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+25 partisan lean makes this one of the most Republican seats in Texas
Tom Sell's lopsided financial edge: $2.5M raised and $1.3M in outside support versus $49K for the Democrat
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 97% to win
No public polling and no expert ratings flag any competitiveness in this open seat
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, an open seat with no incumbent complication, and Tom Sell's overwhelming fundraising advantage leave Democrats without a visible path, and prediction markets agree at about 97% Republican. With no polling suggesting otherwise, Safe R is the clear call.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal involving Sell or a late surge of outside money behind the Democratic nominee would put the result in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's 19th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Representative Jodey Arrington's retirement does little to change that. Republican Tom Sell enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised about $2.5 million and drawn more than $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised roughly $49,000 and has minimal cash on hand. No independent polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee about a 2% chance of winning. The district's R+25 lean, the absence of any visible Democratic campaign infrastructure, and the well-funded Republican consolidation of the open seat all point the same direction. Barring an unforeseen development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin.
